Definition: The share of visits in which the visitor leaves after viewing only one page.
Clicks divided by impressions: how often people who see an item click on it.
The average cost of each click on an advertisement.

Also known as: Cost Per Mille; Cost Per Thousand Impressions
Definition: The cost of showing an advertisement one thousand times.
Revenue earned for each unit of money spent on advertising.
The number of times an advert or piece of content was shown, whether or not anyone looked at it or clicked.
The number of different people who saw the content at least once. Unlike impressions, each person is counted only once.
The average number of times each person in the reach saw the advert. Too high a number can annoy the audience.
The number of times people clicked on an advert, link or button.
The marketing spend divided by the number of leads it produced.

Also known as: CPA; Cost per Action; Cost per Conversion
Definition: The marketing spend divided by the number of customers or actions it won, such as sign-ups or purchases.
The spend divided by the number of times a video was watched past the counting threshold.

Also known as: Landing Page Conversion; Page Conversion Rate
Definition: The share of visitors to a landing page who took the wanted action, such as filling in a form.

Also known as: Marketing Cost; Ad Spend; Media Spend
Definition: The total money spent on marketing activity in a period.
How much of the planned marketing budget has been spent so far, shown as a percentage of the budget.
The profit or revenue gained from marketing compared with what was spent on it.

Also known as: Marketing Attributed Revenue; Marketing Influenced Revenue
Definition: The revenue that can be traced back to marketing activity, such as campaigns that created the lead.
The number of months of customer revenue or margin needed to earn back the cost of winning that customer.
The number of new people or companies who showed interest and left their details in a period.
A score given to each lead showing how likely it is to become a customer, based on who they are and what they have done.

Also known as: Cost per MQL; Cost per SQL
Definition: The marketing spend divided by the number of leads that passed the quality check.
How well a marketing campaign did against its goals, looking at reach, response, leads and sales.
The share of people contacted by a campaign who replied, clicked or took part.
The share of delivered emails that were opened. It shows how well subject lines and send times work.

Also known as: Email Click-Through Rate; Click to Open Rate
Definition: The share of delivered emails in which a link was clicked.
The share of delivered emails that led someone to unsubscribe.
The share of sent emails that reached the inbox rather than bouncing or being blocked.

Also known as: Hard Bounce Rate; Soft Bounce Rate
Definition: The share of sent emails that could not be delivered, for example because the address does not exist.
How fast the email subscriber list is growing, after new sign-ups and unsubscribes are taken into account.
The number of visits to the website in a period.
The number of different people who visited the website in a period, with each person counted once.
The total number of pages opened on the website, including repeat views by the same person.
The average number of pages a visitor looks at in one visit. It is a sign of how engaging the site is.
The average length of a website visit. It is a sign of how long people stay interested.
The share of views of a page that were the last page of the visit.
Visits that came from unpaid search results, without any advertising.
Visits that came from adverts the business paid for.
Visits that arrived by clicking a link on another website.
Visits where the person typed the address in or used a bookmark, so no other source is known.
The number of people who follow the business on a social media account.
The share of the audience that reacted to, commented on, shared or clicked a post, compared with the number who saw it.
The number of times people shared a post with their own contacts.
The business's share of all the advertising or online conversation in its market, compared with competitors.
How many people in the target market know the brand, often measured by survey.
Whether the things people say about the brand online are mostly positive, neutral or negative.
The position at which a page appears in search results for a chosen word or phrase. Position 1 is the top.
Links from other websites to your own. Good ones from trusted sites help the site rank better in search.
The number of times a video was watched past the point that counts as a view.
The share of video starts that were watched to the end.
The share of people who registered for a webinar or event who actually took part.
The number of people who signed up for an event or webinar.
The number of times gated content, such as a guide or report, was downloaded.
How likely people reached by a campaign are to recommend the brand, scored from -100 to 100.
The spend divided by the number of times people interacted with an advert or post.

Term: Return on Ad Spend by Channel
Definition: The revenue earned for each unit spent, shown separately for each channel such as search, social or email.
The way credit for a sale is shared among the marketing activities that the customer came across before buying.
How much a customer is expected to be worth over their lifetime compared with the cost of winning them. A figure of 3 or more is often seen as healthy.
The extra sales produced by a promotion compared with what would have been sold without it.
The share of issued coupons or vouchers that customers actually used.
